seoTitle: How to Add 3 Indicators in TradingView Without Clutter
metaDescription: Add multiple indicators to one TradingView chart, see how they land in separate panes, and what actually happens when you hit your plan's indicator limit.
intro: Stacking indicators can help confirm a setup, but adding three to one chart runs into something most guides skip: TradingView's free Basic plan caps every chart at two indicators. This guide covers searching for and applying indicators, how they land in their own panes automatically, and exactly what happens, plus what your real options are, once you hit that cap.
costNote: TradingView's free Basic plan allows 2 indicators per chart. Essential raises that to 5, Plus to 10, Premium to 25, and Ultimate to 50. A third indicator on one chart is only possible on Essential or above.

steps.heading: Open the Indicators panel and browse or search
steps.body: Click Indicators in the top toolbar to open the panel titled "Indicators, metrics, and strategies." The left column organizes options into Personal (Favorites, My scripts, Invite-only, Purchased), Built-in (Technicals, Fundamentals), and Community (Editors' picks, Top, Trending, Store). Anything starred before shows under Favorites right away; on a fresh account that list starts empty.

image.caption: The Indicators, metrics, and strategies panel, with Favorites selected on the left and Relative Strength Index starred and listed on the right.

steps.heading: Add your first two indicators
steps.body: Search by name; typing part of a word like "volum" brings up every Volume-related indicator, from basic Volume to Volume Weighted Average Price, with the closest match highlighted first. Clicking a result drops it onto the chart immediately. RSI and MACD are common first picks, one reads momentum, the other plots as its own oscillator, and adding both puts each in its own pane below the price chart instead of overlapping.

image.caption: The indicator search showing results for 'volum', with RSI and MACD already added as separate panes beneath the price chart.

steps.heading: Try to add a third indicator on Basic and hit the cap
steps.body: On a free Basic account, a third indicator triggers an upsell panel instead of adding it: "You've applied 2 indicators, the maximum available on your plan," listing RSI and MACD as the two already in use, with Current plan Basic (2) next to Recommended Premium (25). This is a hard cap enforced by the plan, not a setting you can toggle off. It isn't only a Premium-or-nothing choice, though: Essential lifts the cap to 5 and Plus to 10, so a third or fourth indicator doesn't require jumping straight to the most expensive tier.

image.caption: The upgrade prompt shown when adding a third indicator on a Basic plan, listing Basic's 2-indicator cap against a higher tier's limit.

steps.heading: Work within two indicators if you're staying on Basic
steps.body: If upgrading isn't on the table right now, choose the two indicators deliberately instead of trying to squeeze in a third. Pairing a trend tool, a moving average overlaid directly on price, with one oscillator like RSI or MACD covers both trend and momentum without needing a separate pane for a third.

steps.heading: Manage the panes you do have
steps.body: Drag the divider between panes to resize how much vertical space each oscillator gets, and use the eye icon next to an indicator's name to hide it temporarily without deleting it, useful for comparing an RSI-only view against RSI plus MACD without rebuilding the chart each time.

faq.question: How many indicators can I add to one TradingView chart?
faq.answer: It depends on your plan. Basic (free) allows 2 per chart, Essential 5, Plus 10, Premium 25, and Ultimate 50.

faq.question: Why can't I add a third indicator even though the search still works?
faq.answer: Search and add work normally; the limit only shows up when you try to apply the indicator over your plan's cap, and TradingView shows an upgrade prompt instead of adding it. It's a plan-based cap, not a bug.

faq.question: Do I need Premium to get a third indicator?
faq.answer: No. Essential already raises the cap from 2 to 5 indicators per chart. Premium's 25 and Ultimate's 50 only matter if you're running many indicators at once.

faq.question: Should all my indicators go in the same pane?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Moving averages usually overlay directly on price, while oscillators like RSI and MACD are placed in their own panes below the chart automatically.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a walkthrough recorded on a Basic-plan account in August 2025. Plan names and per-chart indicator limits were re-checked against TradingView's official pricing page in September 2026, which corrected an oversimplified upgrade path: the earlier draft framed Premium as the only way past 2 indicators, when Essential (5) and Plus (10) sit between Basic and Premium.
